rows.quote: In all exome-wide analyses, variants were oriented to the protein-increasing allele and exGS were calculated by summing the number of independent (clumping r2 < 0.05, 10,000KB) protein-increasing alleles, weighted by betas reported in Dhindsa et al., and projected in up to 337,543 European UK Biobank participants with exome-sequencing (Supplementary Data 10) using PLINK252.
rows.dataset_named_in_source: 337,543 European UK Biobank participants with exome-sequencing
rows.coder_note: The authors' own analysis of UK Biobank individual-level data (Application Number 67506): the sentence gives the analytic sample and procedure of the genetic cancer analysis (rule C); no dictionary row is this dataset.

The exome pQTL variants are attributed to Dhindsa et al. (entry 44, the 2022 bioRxiv preprint, 50,829 participants); that entry's DOI is no dictionary row's source identifier and 50,829 is not the Dhindsa 2023 row's N (49,736); entry 39 (the Nature paper) is not cited for the dataset, so no entry can carry a code.
